survey: An upright wooden coffin with the classic six-sided outline, standing on its narrow foot end in a grassy field. The front face is one flat panel facing the camera, with a raised wooden cross applied to its upper half. The right-hand side walls show the box's depth. They follow the front outline: a short panel from the top to the shoulder, then a longer tapering panel down to the foot, and a thin strip of the top end is visible. The foot rests flat on the grass, with tufts around the base and a shadow cast behind and to the right, so it reads as grounded. The cross is centred and sits flush on the panel. There are no handles, hinges or lid seam, and leaving out the handles is an acceptable simplification.

errors.where: Front face / side edge of the coffin
errors.what: There is no seam or lip anywhere between the lid and the box. The front panel runs straight into the side walls as one solid block, so the coffin reads as a solid wooden slab that could not be opened. That is its basic function.

fix: Add a visible lid: a thin seam or slightly raised lid panel running around the six-sided outline just inside the edge of the front face, separating the lid from the box walls, so the coffin clearly opens.
